target.title: fix(browser): don't steal focus on headed screenshot captures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Since #100857, `captureScreenshot()` sends `Page.bringToFront` before **every** capture. That guard exists for a headless-specific stall (a backgrounded tab under `--headless=new` never commits a compositor frame, so `Page.captureScreenshot` blocks until the CDP timeout). But on a **headed** browser the same unconditional activation switches the visible tab — and raises the window on some platforms — on every screenshot. Screenshots are the highest-frequency operation in agent browsing loops, so for a headed managed profile (or any browser a human is watching/sharing) the agent constantly steals the user's active tab (#105357).

## Why This Change Was Made

The stall the activation guards against is headless-only, so activation is only needed there. `captureScreenshot` now detects headed-ness via `Browser.getVersion` (the `userAgent` contains `HeadlessChrome` under headless Chrome) and **skips** `Page.bringToFront` only when the browser is confirmed headed. Headless browsers — and any case where detection is unavailable (`Browser.getVersion` fails or returns no userAgent) — keep activating, so the #100857 stall fix is never reintroduced. This is the conservative direction: behavior only changes when we are sure it is safe.

Explicit focus APIs are unaffected; this only removes the *implicit* per-screenshot focus change. (Companion to #105356, which addresses the same focus hygiene for tab creation.)

## User Impact

- On a headed browser, agent screenshots no longer switch the user's visible tab or raise the window.
- Headless capture behavior is unchanged (tab still activated to force a frame).

## Evidence

**Regression tests** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.screenshot-params.test.ts` → 13/13):

- `does not steal focus on a headed browser (#105357)` — headed userAgent → `Page.bringToFront` is **not** sent.
- `still activates the tab on a headless browser (#105357)` — `HeadlessChrome` userAgent → `Page.bringToFront` is sent before capture.
- `activates when headed detection is unavailable (safe default, #105357)` — no userAgent → activation preserved.

**Discriminator**: reverting `cdp.ts` fails the headed test — the unconditional `Page.bringToFront` returns.

Fixes #105357
